That distinction is the difference between the matter and an ARRANGEMENT of it, and this file describes the matter — the packing belongs to whatever assembly holds it. NOT CHARACTERIZED and left at 0: thermal conductivity (strongly porosity-dependent, no single cited figure), latent heats, and any melting or decomposition point — charcoal is largely amorphous carbon and does not melt at 1 atm; it OXIDISES, which is a reaction with its surroundings rather than a property of the substance alone. It is also not a pure substance: composition and properties depend on the parent wood and the pyrolysis conditions, so every number here is a representative value for wood char rather than a constant of nature. ★ REACTION DATA is for the CARBON in it, not for charcoal as sold: C + O2 -> CO2 releases 393.51 kJ/mol (NIST formation enthalpy of CO2), which is 32.8 MJ per kg of pure carbon. Charcoal is typically only 70-90% fixed carbon with the balance volatiles and ash, so its real heating value is lower — the commonly quoted 28-31 MJ/kg. The catalogue stores the exact chemistry and lets a caller scale by carbon fraction, rather than storing a blended number that hides which part is thermodynamics and which is a sample.
